scope: Complete unloaded explanatory rolling stand based on Ms I48v. The fixed roll gap, support journals and modern 20 degree involute tooth profiles are declared assumptions. No metal deformation is simulated.

scale_m.note: Full swept bound. All chosen dimensions are modern explanatory assumptions, never claimed measurements of a historical machine. The 0.92 m Z bound includes the exterior crank grip sweeping to z=-0.454 m.

frame.transforms: All part positions relative to their named parent. Joint q is an extra rotation or translation about the declared parent-frame pivot applied to the rest transform. Children inherit it once.

assumptions.statement: Every numerical part size, position, orientation and support arrangement in parts is a declared modern modelling choice unless a separate primary source is explicitly attached. Materials marked assumed are plausible period choices. They are not measured from any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: Leonardo did not provide a manufacturing drawing with all dimensions.

assumptions.statement: The stated rates and loads are slow modern demonstration choices. They do not reproduce a measured speed in Leonardo s workshop.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating record was located.

assumptions.statement: Gear teeth use the explicit 20 degree involute polygons in parts, module 0.006 m, 20 and 60 teeth. Bore clearances, input shaft and offset crank are modern choices. Rectangular tooth blocks must not replace these profiles.
assumptions.reason: Complete the numerical modern demonstration without presenting invented details as Leonardo dimensions.

input_rate.note: A human turns q-in at5rpm during a12second unloaded demonstration. Lower roller is manually co-turned for this demonstration. It is normally entrained by the tin.

drive.justification: A human turns q-in at5rpm during a12second unloaded demonstration. Lower roller is manually co-turned for this demonstration. It is normally entrained by the tin.

motion.final_hold: At12s hold all joint values. Operator stops cranking.
motion.visitor_12s: One input turn and one third turn of each roller. The lower roller is co-turned by the demonstrator, a declared presentation choice.

animation_notes: No bounce, no hidden energy recharge and no invisible reset.
All independent joints are in the schedule. Rigid descendants follow their parent.
Use the specified SI time without cinematic speed-up.
Show both human inputs as label text. The lower roll cannot rotate by itself without tin contact.
The screw gap adjustment is omitted from animated scope and replaced by fixed period-plausible support blocks. Adjustments require a separate setup.

The 60-tooth wheel has initial local Y phase pi/60, separate from q-upper. This places a tooth opposite a gap at the specified 0.24 m centre distance. The crank is outside the gear plane. The lower roll has separate human input.

research.identification: Ms I48v, Institut de France, verified edition [EL-MILL].
research.sheet_vs_reconstruction: Sheet specifies rollers and metal. IBM Italia1952 supplied a model with adjustable lower supports [MILL-M]. This dossier uses independently chosen dimensions and a fixed gap.
research.dimensions: Quote: “una piastra di stagno larga circa 1/2 braccio” [EL-MILL]. Richter number not verified. Assuming Florentine braccio0.5836m gives width0.2918m. Milan context makes unit selection uncertain, not proof of Florentine usage. No verified Milanese conversion supplied.

claims.tested_by_leonardo: No dated experiment by Leonardo was verified in the sources listed here. This is an evidence gap, not proof that he never tried it.
claims.built_in_lifetime: No lifetime build documented in sources inspected. IBM Italia1952 model is later [MILL-M].
claims.later_tests: No instrumented reduction-force or throughput test located [MILL-M].
